title: Qwen3-Coder
hook: Qwen3-Coder is an open-weight agentic coding model — a 480B Mixture-of-Experts built for long-horizon, tool-using software tasks, rivaling closed models on agentic coding.
key_points: Alibaba's Qwen team, July 2025: open-weight coding models led by Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B.
480B-parameter MoE with 35B active; 256K native context, extendable toward 1M.
Tuned for agentic coding — planning, tool use, and recovering from failed runs.
Reported state-of-the-art among open models on agentic coding, near Claude Sonnet 4.
content_html: Qwen3-Coder, from Alibaba's Qwen team, is an open-weight family of coding models led by Qwen3-Coder-480B-A35B — a 480-billion-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 35 billion parameters active per token. Released in mid-2025, it was tuned specifically for agentic software work: not just autocompleting code, but planning, calling tools, running code, and recovering when things break.
extra_html:
What's new

The flagship model supports a 256K-token context natively and can be extended toward a million tokens — useful for reasoning over whole repositories. Qwen reported state-of-the-art results among open models on agentic coding, browser-use, and tool-use benchmarks, putting it in the conversation with strong closed models like Claude Sonnet 4. Training leaned on large-scale synthesis of verifiable coding tasks paired with executable environments, so the model learns from real execution feedback.

Why it matters

Open-weight coding models that are genuinely agentic — able to drive a multi-step task with tools — narrow one of the most economically important capability gaps with closed labs. Because the weights are downloadable, teams can run Qwen3-Coder privately as the backend for their own coding agents, a major draw for organizations that can't send code to an external API.

related.hook: Qwen3 puts a reasoning switch in one model - a slow 'thinking' mode and a fast 'non-thinking' mode with a controllable budget - across a lineup that runs from 0.6B to a 235B MoE.

related.hook: Fine-tune GPT on public GitHub code and you get a model that solves programming problems and powers GitHub Copilot - plus a new benchmark, HumanEval, that tests functional correctness.
